research_question: How reliably do open-weight instruction-tuned LLMs detect or avoid hallucination across response types and languages?

core_benchmarks.name: HaluEval-QA
core_benchmarks.unit: paired grounded and hallucinated candidate answers
core_benchmarks.scope: all examples in the official QA split

core_benchmarks.name: HalluLens
core_benchmarks.unit: fresh model generations on all official dynamic tasks
core_benchmarks.scope: all generated prompts for all official task scripts

core_benchmarks.name: RAGTruth
core_benchmarks.scope: all good-quality examples in the official test split

core_benchmarks.name: Mu-SHROOM
core_benchmarks.unit: multilingual model response with hallucinated spans
core_benchmarks.scope: all test examples in all official languages; validation is reserved for development

factuality_control.name: TruthfulQA
factuality_control.interpretation: Reported separately because factual accuracy is related to, but not identical with, hallucination.

analysis_rules: Never average task-specific headline metrics into one suite score.
Report every benchmark separately with its sample count and source revision.
Report Mu-SHROOM by language as well as macro and micro aggregates.
Treat command-line sample limits as smoke tests and never as confirmatory results.
Use deterministic decoding and the same model checkpoint across benchmarks.
Do not pool Mu-SHROOM validation examples into the final test metrics.
Record all exclusions and retain row-level predictions for audit.
